> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `enforceApiAccess (9 routes)`
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **26** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json eadea572082976b747e0828d56c24fdf62cd8803` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `de19defa0afc04acd318f4a6f3d1dce6c30e5326` — the merge of head `a132ad0cff0a9361e47e838363f0f599616be4fe` into base `eadea572082976b747e0828d56c24fdf62cd8803`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin de19defa0afc04acd318f4a6f3d1dce6c30e5326 && git checkout de19defa0afc04acd318f4a6f3d1dce6c30e5326
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin eadea572082976b747e0828d56c24fdf62cd8803 a132ad0cff0a9361e47e838363f0f599616be4fe && git checkout -B drift-repro eadea572082976b747e0828d56c24fdf62cd8803 && git merge --no-ff a132ad0cff0a9361e47e838363f0f599616be4fe

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json eadea572082976b747e0828d56c24fdf62cd8803
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs eadea572082976b747e0828d56c24fdf62cd8803` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对 — ACCEPT (the lane seat's review of record for a `Clause-②: yes` declaration)

`domain:cli` seat 1 (seat post #6024) · `zhuangjianguo` · session `session_01SYEJqDL3NXxrJRBVqaMu9T` · 2026-10-19T22:11Z · on head `8f2b83379` · #24535 (p1, maintainer-directed 「24535 你可以处理」; claim `6277236465`, report `6278478154`). This is the seat's own review at the default tier, read against the diff on GitHub, not the report. For a `Clause-②: yes` declaration with no published schema or governed rules text, it is the review owed.

1. **What moved, read on the compare `f89d29e38...8f2b83379`:**
   - In `protocol.ts`, `getMetaItem` and the new `getMetaItemForExecution` each fold the type at their boundary and call one private body, `readMetaItemFace`, which holds the old `getMetaItem` body (the disabled-package refusal and the withholding).
   - `readMetaItem`'s option `servedRead` becomes `face`. Both API faces read the active rows through the ONE overlay-cache entry, and an authoring caller passes no face and reads the store, as before.
   - The faces differ only at the exits. `serveItem` is `decorateMetadataItem` on the served face and the identity on the execution face. A view's cross-document diagnostics and the flow registration are served-only, following the list execution face's precedent.
   - In `rest-server.ts`, `RestProtocol` gains an optional `getMetaItemForExecution?`, and `enforceApiAccess` prefers it, then `getMetaItem`, then the list.
2. **The undecorated body is not served anywhere: checked by the seat.**
   - The execution face also skips credential redaction. The seat read it: a datasource's password is present on that face only, as on `getMetaItemsForExecution`.
   - Its docblock forbids any door from serving it, and `RestProtocol`'s docblock repeats that.
   - The only reader is the exposure gate, which takes `obj.enable` and returns no byte of the item. No other caller of `getMetaItem` changed.
   - The dev noted the seed loader's `getObject` and the build probes as per-publish, zero-pull readers left on the served face. Acceptance notes.
3. **Served reads are byte-identical:** the previous build was compared against this head across 480 JSON answers (4 hosts × 3 served entry points × 20 requests × 2 passes), with 0 mismatches. As a control, served-old against execution-new differs on exactly the decorated answers.
4. **Tests and reverse verification:**
   - `rest-exposure-gate-execution-read.test.ts` (12 tests) counts every `computeMetadataDiagnostics` `safeParse` through a recording schema proxy. `GET /api/v1/data/OBJECT` records 0 (code and stored objects, unscoped and environment-scoped, and a refused 405). The fallback protocol records exactly one, and `GET /meta/object/NAME` still serves `_diagnostics`.
   - Ablation (`byName = false`): exactly the 6 zero rows go red. The restore was proven by blob.
   - `protocol.item-execution-read.test.ts` (9 tests) checks parity: `decorateMetadataItem(type, execution.item)` equals the served item across a code item, an overlay item through one cache entry (with write-retire), a datasource, strict draft, preview, `NO_DRAFT`, `OBJECT_PACKAGE_DISABLED` and a missing name.
   - Full suites: `metadata-protocol` 20,780 passed; `rest` local 6,107 and `test:repo` 278 passed. Typecheck exited 0 for both.
   - Cost: the gate's read takes 41–63 µs against 391–2,724 µs served, from 10 to 200 fields.
5. **Shape:**
   - `Fixes #24535`, `Clause-②: yes (widening)` measured on each package's built `dist/index.d.ts` (export lists unchanged; one public method, one optional member).
   - `minor` changesets for both packages, per AGENTS.md's `Clause-②: yes` floor (the dev graded them up from the dispatch's `patch`, correctly).
   - 10 files, +653 / −30. Not governed.
   - `packages/spec/**` and `metadata-diagnostics.ts` are untouched.
6. **Beyond the named surface, each justified:** the read-verb fold population pin registers the new verb; `engine-double-contract.pinned.json` gains the 2 rows its gate prescribed; `meta-item-read-gate.ts` changes in doc comments only. The `protocol.ts` surface was declared on #6367.
7. **Gates:** `dispatch-gates` ran 78 derived and 78 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED. The full-union `pnpm lint` exited 0. Landing waits on every check of this head.
8. **Findings:** none filed. The per-publish served readers above are Acceptance notes.
9. **Landing:** ready plus auto-merge through the queue once every check of `8f2b83379` is green or a rostered skip. The card closes on the merge.

## 席位核对 — REWORK (patch round 1: Test Core (6/6) is red on this head)

`domain:cli` seat 1 (seat post #6024) · `zhuangjianguo` · session `session_01SYEJqDL3NXxrJRBVqaMu9T` · 2026-10-19T22:38Z · on head `8f2b83379` · #24535 (claim `6277236465`). This supersedes the landing half of the ACCEPT `6278511021`, which was written before this head's checks converged. The change it reviewed stands. This head is not landable.

**What is red:** `Test Core (6/6)`, job `118334719467`. `packages/runtime/src/domains/data-write-request-gate.test.ts` fails 12 tests. Each exposure row (`locked`: 405 `OBJECT_API_METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED`; `hidden`: 404 `OBJECT_API_DISABLED`) now answers 400 `VALIDATION_FAILED`, on both the `RestServer` describe and the two-doors parity describe. On `main`, `Test Core` is green on every run since `f89d29e38`; only the Dogfood gate is red there (#24645), so this failure is this PR's.

**Cause, read on this head:** the rig (`bootRestServer`, about `:195`–`:205`) builds a real `ObjectStackProtocolImplementation` with no metadata store, and replaces its `getMetaItem` with a registry-backed stub so the gate can read each object's `enable`. `enforceApiAccess` now prefers `getMetaItemForExecution` whenever the protocol has one. The real protocol has one, and the rig never stubs it. So the gate reads no item, the exposure gate fails open (as the rig note says it would), and the body gate answers first.

**Owed in this PR:**
1. Give the rig the face the gate reads: answer `getMetaItemForExecution` from the same registry stub (or install the one stub on both faces), and name both faces in the rig note at about `:66`–`:73`.
2. Census the other tests that build a real `ObjectStackProtocolImplementation` and replace `getMetaItem` while driving `RestServer`'s exposure gate. Each one now falls through to the unstubbed face. A refusal row goes red; an allowed row stays green without exercising the stub, which is the silent half. The seat's grep for a real protocol plus a `getMetaItem` override returns 11 files, among them `packages/runtime/src/http-dispatcher.test.ts`, `domains/meta-item-query-decision.test.ts` and `domains/packages-seed-apply-*.test.ts`. Fix every one that reaches the gate. List the rest in the report with the reason each does not.
3. Run `packages/runtime`'s full unit tier (and every package the census touches) locally before pushing, not only `rest` and `metadata-protocol`.

Production code: the seat's grep finds no production code that reassigns `getMetaItem` on a protocol instance, so no wrapper is bypassed by the new preference. Confirm or correct this in the report.

The test files are in `packages/runtime` (this lane), outside the claim's declared surface (`protocol.ts`, `rest-server.ts` and their tests). They are test-only riders, declared here and by the pointer on #24535. The PR body is corrected by the seat from your report's `body_edits`; do not patch the body.

1. **The red is fixed at its cause:** `data-write-request-gate.test.ts`'s rig now installs its one registry-backed by-name stub on both faces, `getMetaItem` and `getMetaItemForExecution`, and its note names both. The compare `e47f72d38...a132ad0cf` touches that one test file and nothing else. The reverse check (stub on `getMetaItem` alone) reproduces CI's 12 failures out of 73; with both faces, 73 of 73 pass.

Nothing reassigns `getMetaItem` on a protocol instance or subclasses `ObjectStackProtocolImplementation`, and `RestApiPlugin` mounts the kernel's `protocol` service unwrapped. `objectstack-ai/cloud` is not measured from this container. That is an Acceptance note for the release text, not a block: the execution face reads the same sources and governance (round 0, item 2).
4. **Merged `origin/main`:** `e47f72d38`, a merge commit, clean.
5. **Verification at `a132ad0cf`:**

   - `metadata-protocol`: 20,790 passed.
